title: Solar Production vs Home Consumption
dataSources: SolarEdge/Enphase production (`solaredge:power`, `enphase:production`), Powerwall (`powerwall:aggregate`), smart-meter P1/DSMR (`dsmr:telegram`), Emporia Vue (`emporia:circuit`).
app: Solar inverters (SolarEdge/Enphase/Fronius/Growatt), Tesla Powerwall, and smart meters (P1/DSMR, Emporia Vue, Sense) via vendor APIs and MQTT to HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=solaredge:power
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(production_wh) as produced, sum(consumption_wh) as consumed by _time
| eval self_sufficiency_pct=round(100*min(produced,consumed)/consumed,1)
| sort - _time
description: Compares how much energy your solar panels produced with how much your home used each day and calculates your self-sufficiency percentage.
value: Self-sufficiency is the number that makes solar feel worthwhile; tracking it daily shows the payback and reveals your best and worst days.
implementation: Ingest inverter production and meter consumption; schedule daily and trend your self-sufficiency percentage.
visualization: Chart of daily production versus consumption with a self-sufficiency line.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how much power your solar panels made with how much your home used, so you can see how self-sufficient you are.
